text:
Marat Khusnutdinov hasn't touched the scoresheet since late October, ten straight games without a point while we'd have expected about 3.5 at his ice time. That would be easy to wave off as bad luck if the chances were still there. They mostly aren't: the looks with him on the ice have thinned out a little, and the ones he does get aren't going in. Some of each, in other words.

The season line is 3 goals and 6 points in 22 games on 14 minutes a night. Boston still gets about 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, so his shifts aren't sinking anyone. He's quick, with his bursts over 20 mph in the top 13% of the league, but his top shot speed sits near the bottom fifth, which means he has to get close to beat a goalie.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins last season, 79th among forwards, mostly from even-strength offense, and he put up 33 points. The 24-year-old has a better version of this season in him. What we'd watch is whether the minutes hold while he looks for it.
